Subject: Re: PII handling for prompts/outputs — confirmation and controls

Hi Alex / team — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, written confirmation you can use in your risk review. I’ve kept the language explicit and included available options for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments. I’m also attaching a short summary PDF and the standard DPA/SOC2 links.

Short answers (high-level):
- Storage of prompts/outputs: By default, Redwood’s Hosted API retains request and response payloads for up to 30 days for debugging, abuse detection, and service quality. These payloads are considered customer data.
- Configurable retention: Retention is configurable per-customer. We offer: 30 days (default), custom windows (e.g., 0 days / no retention), and extended retention for audit requirements. All changes require a signed amendment for Hosted customers; Dedicated and Private customers can set retention via account settings and API.
- Option to disable storage: Yes. For Dedicated and Private deployments, customers can opt to disable prompt/output storage; for Hosted customers, we can set retention to 0 and disable logging of payloads at the account level (enterprise plan/contracted change).
- Data residency and storage location: Data is stored in the region you select for your account. For US customers we store in the selected AWS region (e.g., us-west-2). For EU customers we store in eu-west-1 or the selected EU region. Dedicated/Private deployments can be deployed into your VPC/region to guarantee residency.
- Encryption and key management: All stored customer data is encrypted at rest (AES-256). By default we manage keys via cloud KMS. We offer customer-managed keys (CMK) for Dedicated and Private deployments and, for some enterprise Hosted plans, as an add-on.
- No training on customer data: Redwood does not use customer prompt/response payloads to train or improve our public models. Data retained for debugging/abuse detection is accessible to a limited internal SRE/security group under strict access controls and is only used for the stated operational purposes.
- Redaction and hashing options: We provide a redaction API and request/response hashing so teams can store only non-PII derivatives (hashes, metadata). We can also provide automatic PII redaction at ingestion as a managed option.
- Audit logs: We persist audit logs (operation/authorization events) for 365 days by default; longer retention available on request. Audit logs include request IDs and metadata but not full payloads unless retention is enabled for debugging.
- Access controls & attestation: Role-based access controls, SSO integration (SAML/OIDC), granular IAM for Dedicated deployments, and regular access reviews. We can provide an access attestation export on request.

Practical examples for FinPay:
- If you want zero chance of Redwood retaining any prompts/outputs, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment with retention set to 0 and CMK enabled.
- If you prefer Hosted but need short retention, we can set Hosted account retention to 0 (contract amendment) or 7 days as an interim.

Attachments included: redwood-pii-handling-summary.pdf (policy and config options) and pointer to SOC2 report & DPA template: https://redwood.app.link/security/soc2-report and https://redwood.app.link/legal/dpa

Next steps I propose:
1) Rishi/Marissa: confirm whether FinPay prefers Hosted (with a retention amendment) or Dedicated/Private.
2) If Hosted + retention=0 is acceptable, we’ll initiate an amendment and schedule a short tech call to validate request flows.
3) If Dedicated/Private: we’ll put together a deployment plan and CMK onboarding checklist.

Let me know if you want a short tech deep-dive this week; I can bring a runtime engineer for details on redaction and log scrubbing.

 Neha Kapoor
